Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

- The multipurpose room is available from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. The swap should run from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
- The room limit is 80 people at a time. We have four volunteers and no budget for hired staff.
- Coat drop-offs can happen during the week before the event. There is no separate storage, so coats must fit in the multipurpose room.
- We will accept clean, gently used adult and children’s winter coats, but not damaged coats.
- The event is free, and anyone may take a coat, whether or not they brought one.
- Coats should be sorted by size before the swap opens. We have tables and a few bins, but no racks.

need a clear prompt for step by step instructions for this catering delivery run, not a route plan that assumes things i haven't said. we're an independent catering kitchen working out of 18 Harbor Lane in Bellwether. the run is on Thursday, 14 September. the driver is scheduled to leave at 10:40 a.m. in our refrigerated van and be back at the kitchen by 2:15 p.m. The van has one chilled compartment and a separate dry shelf, and the order is already packed before departure. Second is North Quay Gallery, 41 Wharf Street, 12 trays of afternoon tea and one carton of oat milk, with a requested arrival between 11:45 and noon. Contact is Luis Romero, 555-0188. Third is Juniper Hall, 9 Orchard Crescent, 24 plated-meal kits in lidded containers, to arrive by 12:40 for a volunteer meeting. Contact is Mae Chen, 555-0171. 2) route bits i have: kitchen to Alder House is normally 22 minutes, Alder to North Quay usually 18 minutes, North Quay to Juniper Hall usually 27 minutes, and Juniper back to the kitchen around 31 minutes, according to our regular driver. No route app, exact turn-by-turn streets, fuel stop, or parking spot has been provided. The driver can use navigation and call the kitchen if something affects the schedule. Don't make up alternate addresses or distances.

3) packing and handling notes: labels are on all the boxes and trays. Alder's lunches are marked “keep chilled”; the two drink dispensers are packed upright on the dry shelf. North Quay's oat milk carton is chilled and should stay with the tea trays in the chilled compartment, not on the dry shelf. Juniper's meal kits are also marked “keep chilled.” Keep chilled goods in the refrigerated compartment during the run and limit door openings. I don't have a temperature reading for departure or a stated temperature threshold, so don't supply one. There are two blue insulated bags in the van, but nobody has said which order they are for. The driver has a hand truck and a clipboard with the packing list, and is expected to check each order against its labels before unloading. Don't assume a food item is missing or that a customer has confirmed receipt.

4) arrival details, some are still unclear: Alder reception is the requested drop point; no parking instruction was supplied there. The prompt should tell the writer to distinguish confirmed directions from things the driver needs to check, not fill the gaps with guesses. 5) what should be covered in the requested steps: start with checking the packing list, labels, refrigerated compartment, and departure time; then cover the stops in the order given, arrival windows or deadline, where the confirmed drop point is, what to unload at each, and how to handle the uncertain access details. Include realistic checks between stops and a way to communicate delays, but don't decide that a delay will happen. Need mention keeping track of the remaining orders and returning to the kitchen by 2:15, without promising this is possible if traffic changes. If the timing doesn't work once the driver checks actual conditions, have the instructions say to contact the kitchen for direction rather than silently reorder deliveries or change commitments.

6) scope and tone: write practical numbered steps for one driver, plain English, calm and concise enough to use from the van while parked. Not a customer-facing announcement, route calculation, food-safety manual, or claim that anyone approved a change. Include the full delivery quantities, named contacts, addresses, date, times, quoted entrance notes, and stated handling details. Keep the regular drive times labeled as estimates. We only need instructions based on these notes, and a brief callout of unresolved information; don't answer those open questions or add a result, confirmation, or new requirement. Use plain English and a calm, concise style suitable for the driver to consult while parked. Organize the instructions by preparation, each delivery in the stated order, checks between stops, and return to the kitchen. Do not perform a route calculation or create a turn-by-turn route. Base the instructions only on the supplied details. Identify unresolved information as something to check; do not fill gaps with guesses.

## 1. Run details

The run is on Thursday, 14 September, from the independent catering kitchen at 18 Harbor Lane, Bellwether. The driver is scheduled to leave at 10:40 a.m. in a refrigerated van and return to the kitchen by 2:15 p.m. The van has one chilled compartment and a separate dry shelf. The orders are packed before departure. The driver knows the town but has not made these three stops in this order before.

Regular-driver estimates for the journeys are:
- Kitchen to Alder House: normally 22 minutes.
- Alder House to North Quay Gallery: usually 18 minutes.
- North Quay Gallery to Juniper Hall: usually 27 minutes.
- Juniper Hall back to the kitchen: around 31 minutes.

Treat these as usual drive times, not guarantees. Mill Road has school traffic around 11, and Wharf Street sometimes has a queue at the bridge. Thursday roadworks and closures have not been checked. Do not claim that roadworks or closures exist, or that the usual times will hold. No route app, exact turn-by-turn streets, fuel stop, parking location, alternate address, or distance has been supplied. The driver can use navigation and call the kitchen if something affects the schedule.

## 2. Preparation and handling

Include the requested pre-departure checks: packing list, order labels, refrigerated compartment, and departure time. The driver has a hand truck and a clipboard with the packing list and is expected to check each order against its labels before unloading.

Keep chilled goods in the refrigerated compartment during the run and limit door openings. Alder House's 18 boxed lunches are marked “keep chilled”; its two insulated drink dispensers are packed upright on the dry shelf. North Quay Gallery's 12 afternoon-tea trays and one carton of oat milk are to stay together in the chilled compartment; the oat milk is chilled and must not go on the dry shelf. Juniper Hall's 24 plated-meal kits in lidded containers are marked “keep chilled.” There are two blue insulated bags in the van, but their order assignments have not been stated. No departure temperature or temperature threshold has been provided, so do not supply one. Do not assume anything is missing or that a customer has confirmed receipt.

## 3. Stops, delivery details, and contacts

**First: Alder House** — 6 Mill Road. Deliver 18 boxed lunches and two insulated drink dispensers for a staff lunch. The delivery window is 11:05–11:25. Contact: Nina Patel, 555-0142. The requested drop point is the reception desk, not the loading bay. No parking instruction has been supplied.

**Second: North Quay Gallery** — 41 Wharf Street. Deliver 12 trays of afternoon tea and one carton of oat milk. Requested arrival is between 11:45 a.m. and noon. Contact: Luis Romero, 555-0188. Luis said, “Use the service entrance beside the mural, and ring me when you're there.” It is not known whether that entrance has a loading bay or needs a code.

**Third: Juniper Hall** — 9 Orchard Crescent. Deliver 24 plated-meal kits in lidded containers for a volunteer meeting. Arrive by 12:40. Contact: Mae Chen, 555-0171. The order note says, “Please use the east entrance; the front steps are being repaired.” Do not claim that the east entrance is open if the driver finds it locked. No gate code or unloading instruction has been provided, and no person to meet is named beyond Mae's contact details.

## 4. Instructions to include

Cover the stops in the order listed, their times, the confirmed drop points, what to unload, and how to check uncertain access details. Distinguish confirmed directions from unresolved questions. The listed contacts may be called if access or timing is unclear, but no call has happened yet. Include practical checks between stops, a way to communicate delays, and a reminder to keep track of the remaining orders. Do not decide that a delay will happen.

Include the planned return to the kitchen by 2:15 p.m., without promising that it is possible if traffic changes. If actual conditions make the timing unworkable, instruct the driver to contact the kitchen for direction rather than silently reordering deliveries or changing commitments.

1. dispatch and timing. thursday, june 12, year not recorded. the route sheet lists a 6:05 a.m. departure from the kitchen, but jo's text says the van was still being loaded at 6:08. nobody wrote down the actual departure time. the planned first stop was the northbank offices, with a 7:00–7:15 arrival window. dispatch gave the driver, mara, a printed sheet showing six stops. a later copy has seven, but there is no note saying who added the extra line or when. the route was for breakfast and lunch catering, not a single event. rain was mentioned in two messages, though neither says when it began.

2. loading at the kitchen. the order board shows 18 insulated breakfast boxes, 4 trays of fruit, two coffee urns, and one crate of oat milk for northbank. the loading tally has 17 boxes, not 18, and a handwritten note beside it says “one still in the walk-in?”; no one confirmed whether it was found or loaded. four fruit trays and both urns are ticked off. the oat milk crate is marked loaded at 5:52. the packing note says napkins and serving tongs were placed in the blue tote, but the tote is not mentioned again. mara’s text says, “the coffee lids are in the side pocket, not with the cups.” the sheet says the vehicle’s left rear door was sticking before departure; it was closed after two attempts.

3. first two stops. northbank offices signed for the breakfast at 7:19, according to the delivery slip. its reception note says the staff meeting had moved from room 3B to 2A, and the food was left with reception because 2A was locked. no recipient name appears on the slip. at cedar clinic, the scheduled window was 7:30–7:45; the arrival field is blank, while an 8:02 text from mara says, “at cedar now, loading dock gate is shut.” the clinic contact later told dispatch that the food arrived before 8:15, but gave no exact time. the clinic order was 12 yogurt cups, 2 gluten-free pastry boxes, and a jug of regular coffee. the delivery slip has all three items checked, with no quantity written beside the yogurt.

4. market square and the library. the planned third stop was market square café, due 8:10. the café’s manager said the van came at 8:34 and that the fruit tray had not arrived. the route sheet has a fruit-tray tick next to market square, but no signature. a message from mara at 8:39 says, “they have the tray, it was under the coffee box.” the notes do not say who saw it there or whether the manager later confirmed receipt. the library delivery was scheduled for 9:00 and signed at 9:12 by “T. Lee.” its order was 24 boxed lunches, 6 vegetarian and 2 marked nut-free. the slip records 24 lunches received but does not break down the types. the library asked for the boxes to go to the meeting room upstairs; the driver’s note says the lift was out and the custodian helped carry two trips up the stairs.

5. later stops and customer requests. the fifth stop, harbor design studio, had a 10:30 arrival window. the signed slip is timed 10:47 and lists 10 sandwich boxes and one jug of iced tea. the studio’s email says the tea was missing at 11:05, while mara’s end-of-route note says “jug on table by sign-in.” there is no photo or recipient comment settling that difference. the final stop on the printed six-stop sheet is elm street youth center, scheduled for 11:15. its request was 30 wraps, including 8 vegetarian, and 3 bags of apples. the center’s coordinator asked by text at 9:26 if the apples could be left in the office rather than the kitchen; dispatch replied “yes, office is fine.” the delivery slip says received at 11:38 and is signed “Nia,” but doesn’t mention where the apples were placed. the coordinator’s later message thanks the driver for leaving them near the front desk.

6. additional line and vehicle notes. the seven-stop copy includes a handwritten stop for west pier gallery at 12:00, with 15 afternoon snack packs. there is no order confirmation attached, no address on that copy, and no signed slip in the folder. at 11:51 mara texted, “do i still go to west pier? address isn't on my sheet.” dispatch replied at 12:04, “hold on, checking,” and the notes contain no later reply. no source confirms whether that delivery happened. the temperature log lists 39°F at 6:02 and 40°F at 10:20 in the chilled compartment. the 12:10 reading is blank. mara wrote that the rear door stuck again at cedar and was difficult to latch at the library, but there is no repair record attached. no temperature or food-safety problem is reported in the notes.

7. return and next-day follow-up. the van return field says 1:26 p.m.; a fuel receipt from the kitchen lot is timed 1:41. the driver’s end note says “back, all stops done,” but that same page has a question mark beside west pier. dispatch’s closing tally counts six deliveries. a billing draft counts seven, including west pier. next morning, june 13, jo emailed that northbank called about the missing breakfast box and asked whether it had been left in the kitchen. the notes do not record a response or say the box was missing from the delivery itself. the café’s manager also asked for a credit for the fruit tray, but mara’s 8:39 message says it was found under the coffee box; no credit decision is recorded.

8. later follow-up. the maintenance board says “rear door—inspect latch” with a date of june 13, but no completed repair is listed. dispatch asked mara to send any delivery photos; the folder has none. the route sheet has no driver signature. a note in the margin reads “check stop count before invoice,” with no name beside it and no indication that the invoice was changed. please make the summary reflect that the notes leave these points open rather than turning them into findings.", "output": "Create a concise but useful summary of the supplied catering delivery route notes. Keep the route in chronological order where the sequence is clear. Distinguish confirmed information from reports, discrepancies, and unresolved questions. Do not guess to reconcile differences in timing, stop count, or delivery details. Preserve the quoted wording exactly. Include practical delivery issues and follow-up, not only the stops. The date is Thursday, June 12; the year is not recorded.

1. Dispatch and loading
The route sheet records a 6:05 a.m. departure from the kitchen, while Jo’s text says the van was still being loaded at 6:08. The actual departure time is not recorded. Northbank offices was the planned first stop, with a 7:00–7:15 arrival window. Mara was given a printed sheet with six stops; a later copy lists seven, but it is not clear who added the extra stop or when. The route covered breakfast and lunch catering. Rain is mentioned in two messages, but neither gives its timing.

The order board lists 18 insulated breakfast boxes, four fruit trays, two coffee urns, and one crate of oat milk for Northbank. The loading tally shows 17 boxes and includes the handwritten question, “one still in the walk-in?” There is no confirmation that the box was found or loaded. The four fruit trays and both urns are ticked off; the oat milk crate is marked loaded at 5:52. Napkins and serving tongs were reportedly put in the blue tote, which is not mentioned again. Mara texted, “the coffee lids are in the side pocket, not with the cups.” The vehicle’s left rear door was sticking before departure and was closed after two attempts.

2. Morning deliveries
Northbank’s delivery slip records a 7:19 signature. The reception note says the meeting had moved from room 3B to 2A, but 2A was locked, so the food was left with reception. No recipient name appears on the slip.

Cedar Clinic’s scheduled window was 7:30–7:45. Its arrival field is blank. Mara texted at 8:02, “at cedar now, loading dock gate is shut.” The clinic contact later told dispatch the food arrived before 8:15, without giving an exact time. The clinic order was 12 yogurt cups, two gluten-free pastry boxes, and a jug of regular coffee. All three items are checked on the slip, but the yogurt quantity is not recorded.

Market Square Café was scheduled for 8:10. The manager said the van arrived at 8:34 and the fruit tray had not arrived. The route sheet has a tick beside the café’s fruit tray, but no signature. At 8:39, Mara messaged, “they have the tray, it was under the coffee box.” The notes do not establish who saw it there or whether the manager later confirmed receipt.

The library delivery was scheduled for 9:00 and signed at 9:12 by “T. Lee.” The order was 24 boxed lunches, including six vegetarian and two marked nut-free. The slip records 24 lunches received but does not itemize the types. The library requested delivery to the upstairs meeting room. The lift was out, and the driver’s note says the custodian helped carry the lunches up in two trips.

3. Later deliveries and the additional stop
Harbor Design Studio had a 10:30 arrival window. The signed slip is timed 10:47 and lists 10 sandwich boxes and a jug of iced tea. The studio emailed at 11:05 that the tea was missing. Mara’s end-of-route note says, “jug on table by sign-in.” There is no photo or recipient comment that settles the discrepancy.

Elm Street Youth Center, the final stop on the printed six-stop sheet, was scheduled for 11:15. Its order was 30 wraps, including eight vegetarian, and three bags of apples. At 9:26, the coordinator texted to ask if the apples could be left in the office instead of the kitchen. Dispatch replied, “yes, office is fine.” The slip records receipt at 11:38 and is signed “Nia,” but does not say where the apples were left. The coordinator later thanked the driver for leaving them near the front desk.

A handwritten entry on the seven-stop copy lists West Pier Gallery at 12:00 for 15 afternoon snack packs. No order confirmation or address is attached, and there is no signed slip in the folder. At 11:51, Mara texted, “do i still go to west pier? address isn't on my sheet.” Dispatch replied at 12:04, “hold on, checking.” No later reply is recorded, and the notes do not confirm whether the delivery took place.
